sections.h2: How fast can a Dania Beach house sell?
sections.html:
Speed here depends mostly on who is paying. A cash buyer needs a title search and a signed contract. A buyer with a mortgage adds an appraisal and loan approval to the list.

The city covers about 7.81 square miles, so one city hall, one appraiser and one clerk of court handle almost every step.

  • An agent exposes the house to the most buyers and takes the most time.
  • Selling it yourself saves the commission, but you handle pricing, paperwork and disclosures.
  • A cash buyer accepts deferred repairs, which suits inherited, rented or worn-out homes.

Owners occupy fewer than half of Dania Beach's homes, 46.8 percent for 2020-2024, so the house next door is as likely to be a rental as an owner's home.

The home value comes from answers across the whole city. Condos, mobile homes, bungalows and newer townhomes all feed one number, so treat it as background and ask for a local comparison on your own street.

About 4,061.8 people live in each square mile, and 86.9% of residents kept the same address from one year to the next, a sign of settled blocks. Median household income is $52,748, which sets the range many buyers can afford. Of residents five and older, 43.7% speak something other than English at home.

That suggests two practical moves. Put your listing in more than one language, and mention road access, since the average commute is 28.4 minutes. A disabled veteran may also qualify for the state's assessment reduction, which a buyer's agent may bring up.

The city calls itself Broward's First City, and its historic properties page lists buildings from the 1910s through the 1950s: the Nyberg-Swanson House (circa 1912), the Bank of Dania and the Martin C. Frost Residence (both 1923), Hotel Poinciana (1926) and the Dania Library and Woman's Club (1935).

Old blocks tend to have old systems. An inspector or insurer looks first at the roof, panel, plumbing runs and windows, and a house that has not been touched is where an as-is sale makes the most sense. If yours is listed or next to a listed property, ask the planning and zoning staff about exterior changes before you talk renovation with a buyer.

A stay of short duration needs a city certificate. Owners apply for a Vacation Rental Certificate through the Planning and Zoning Division of Community Development, and the website explains the application.

Longer leases fall under chapter 83 of the Florida Statutes, which applies to every landlord in the state.

  • Late rent calls for a written demand giving three days, not counting weekends and court holidays.
  • A month-to-month tenant receives thirty days' notice before the period ends.
  • Only the sheriff can remove an occupant, after a judge rules and a writ issues.

A tenant does not stop a sale. Some buyers will close with the occupant still in place, so raise that option before you begin an eviction you may not need.

sections.h2: Permits and code items that slow a closing
sections.html:
Open permits and unfinished work are the usual snags. The city's Community Development Department can pull the records for your address.

A roof, water heater, window or addition that never had a final inspection can show up in a buyer's title or insurance review. Closing an old permit usually costs less than a later price cut. Ask the city for a lien search as well, so any unpaid charge is known well before closing.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html:
Round up your deed, your latest Broward tax bill, permit records, a lender payoff statement and your insurance declarations page. If an association governs the property, add its rules and a current balance statement.

Next, walk the house with a critical eye. Buyers of older homes usually check the roof, electrical panel, plumbing and windows before paint. Write down what you know about each, including dates of past repairs.

Last, decide ahead of time what you will do if the first offer is lower than you hoped. Knowing your minimum, your carrying costs and your deadline keeps a short timeline from becoming a rushed one.

sections.h2: Broward tax calendar and the cap
sections.html:
Broward County bills on a state-set schedule. Your house is valued on January 1, a notice of proposed taxes follows in August, and the tax collector mails bills in November.

  • Exemption forms must reach the appraiser by March 1.
  • The discount shrinks each month, starting at 4 percent for November.
  • April 1 begins delinquency, and certificate sales wrap up by June 1.
  • Value disputes go to the clerk within 25 days of the August notice.

A sale ends the Save Our Homes cap. The buyer's assessment starts at just value on the next New Year's Day, so your old bill often understates what they will owe.

Moving within Florida? Portability can carry over part of your capped benefit if the new homestead is set up within three years of the first January 1 after you left the old one. File form DR-501T with your DR-501 by March 1.

sections.h2: If the house is inherited or in default
sections.html:
An inherited house goes through probate first, because the personal representative needs court authority before signing a deed. Summary administration, a shorter route, is open to estates of $150,000 or less and to deaths more than two years past.

After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk schedules a public sale 20 to 35 days out unless the lender agrees to wait. A private sale that closes sooner repays the loan and leaves any surplus with you.

Unpaid taxes run on a separate clock, since a certificate holder may seek a tax deed once two years have passed from April 1 of the issue year. Your title company quotes the payoff when the sale opens.

faqs.q: Do I need to close an old permit before listing in Dania Beach?
faqs.a: The law does not require it, but an open permit can stall a closing. Ask Community Development whether anything is open on your parcel and request a lien search before you sign.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Dania Beach home?
faqs.a: The Broward clerk records it, and the title company usually handles recording and the state's deed tax at closing.

faqs.q: When do Broward early-payment discounts end?
faqs.a: February is the last discount month, at 1 percent. After that the full amount is due, and unpaid bills are delinquent from April 1.

faqs.q: Can a Dania Beach house be sold with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer may accept the lease, or you can give thirty days' written warning on a monthly tenancy. Changing the locks yourself is not allowed.

faqs.q: Does a Dania Beach sale reset the property tax cap?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of ownership returns assessed value to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's bill can run well above yours. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the property appraiser about portability.
